# Frontier reset: scientific checkpoint, 7 October2026

The strongest research-enabling advance is a smaller explicit detector and exact learner for finite-state noncommutative algebraic models. The strongest separate foundational lead is a threshold-repetition theorem for arbitrary commuting-operator strategies. Both have complete written derivations and multiple internal reconstructions. Neither has external validation, compiled formal verification or established historical novelty. No revolutionary breakthrough is claimed.

## 1. Exact representation acquisition

For n symbols and a proper characteristic-zero recognizable series with at most m hidden states, let T_i be the explicit Volterra matrices of dimension2nm. Our new theorem is

    f !=0  implies  f(ell T_1,...,ell T_n)!=0
    for some integer ell in {1,...,m}.

All evaluations exist because the matrices are jointly strictly lower triangular. This is a universal deterministic hitting set whose construction reads only n,m. One direct-sum tuple has dimension2nm². The prior construction in this cycle used a length marker of dimension approximately n²m⁴. For acyclic representations, one unscaled tuple of dimension2nm already suffices when its full matrix output is read.

The proof uses the released finite-word hyperlogarithm independence, but replaces its scalar multiplicity argument with a bivariate Volterra kernel. A covariant rational row-span argument finds a nonzero diagonal derivative before order m. Degree bounds and Cauchy interpolation make it visible in dimension2nm. A new scalar-parameter degree bound then reduces cyclic faithfulness to m fixed rescalings. This last step was derived by root and independently reconstructed by four workers. Root also reconstructed the complete primary monodromy proof of finite-word independence.

The boundary is equally concrete. The nonzero proper series

    AB-B(I+A)^-1A(I+B)

has leading commutator AB-BA, yet vanishes on the unscaled Volterra operators J_1,J_2 on EVERY formal input, and hence at every finite truncation. Increasing the matrix size cannot repair that cyclic alias. Scalar grading supplies the missing information.

# Spectral threshold repetition in the commuting-operator model

Status: COMPLETE_INTERNAL_DERIVATION; independent operator/game gate by
frontier_quantum_bridge and a third full adversarial reconstruction by
frontier_functional both PASS on the stated interface. No external
validation, formal verification, or historical novelty certificate is claimed.
This changes the source's strategy interface; it is not an automatic
corollary obtained by identifying commuting and finite tensor models.

## Question, assumptions and theorem

Let G be a finite two-player one-round game, with classical finite question
sets X,Y, finite nonempty answer sets A,B, known law mu on X times Y and
Boolean acceptance V. A commuting strategy consists of a Hilbert space H,
a unit vector psi, and POVMs M_x^a,N_y^b on H with

    [M_x^a,N_y^b]=0 for EVERY x,y,a,b.

H may be infinite dimensional; it need not carry a tensor factorization
or a trace. Define omega^co(G) as the supremum of
sum mu(x,y)V(x,y,a,b)<psi,M_x^a N_y^b psi> over these strategies.
The corresponding repeated strategy has arbitrary joint local POVMs for
the complete question/answer strings, subject to the same cross
commutation condition.

This value agrees with the conventional projective-measurement commuting
value. An explicit dilation that preserves all cross commutators is given
in Section 7 below. This equivalence changes the measurement description
within the commuting model; it does not identify that model with finite
tensor-product entanglement.

On the positive-mass pair graph H_mu, adjacent pairs share a local input.
For every non-singleton component j put mu_j=mu(.|j),
P_j=(P_X+P_Y)/2 on L2(mu_j), and

    sigma_j=gap(I-P_j on the orthogonal complement of constants).

Take sigma=min_j sigma_j, with sigma=1 if all components are singletons.
Connectedness and finiteness ensure sigma>0. All logarithms are natural.

**Internally derived theorem.** For v=omega^co(G)<1, 0<delta<1-v,
k>=1, and every commuting strategy for the independent k-fold questions,

# A third internal audit of commuting spectral repetition

Scientific verdict: **PASS on the stated arbitrary commuting-strategy interface**.
I independently reconstructed the load-bearing operator, exposure, barycenter,
component-drift and short-length arguments, and found no hidden finite-rank,
tensor-factorization, trace, or lower-spectrum assumption after the explicit
bounded-form repairs. This is an internal mathematical proof audit, not
external validation, a Lean certificate, or a literature-priority certificate.

Proposed theorem and assembling proof:
`notes/frontier_check_repetition/cycle19/COMMUTING_THRESHOLD_EXTENSION.md`.
The earlier operator gate is
`notes/frontier_quantum_bridge/cycle19/COMMUTING_RESOLVENT_INDEPENDENT_GATE.md`.
This audit read both notes in full, the spectral precursor in full, and the
pinned source's operator, mixed-exposure, marginal and threshold sections in
full. The source's unrelated Song-dependent universal theorem is not used.

## 1. Exact interface and theorem checked

Let `G` be a finite two-player one-round game with finite classical questions,
nonempty finite answers `A,B`, law `μ`, and Boolean acceptance predicate.
A strategy is a unit vector `ψ` on any Hilbert space `H` and local POVMs
whose Alice and Bob effects commute for **every** pair of local inputs and
answers. Their generated von Neumann algebras `𝒜,ℬ` commute. Set
`v=ωᶜᵒ(G)<1`, taking the supremum over all such representations and vectors.
The repeated strategy may use arbitrary joint string POVMs.

On each positive support component of the pair graph (pairs joined by a
shared local question), use the conditional-expectation projections `P_X,P_Y`
on `L²(μ_j)`, and define `P_j=(P_X+P_Y)/2`. Let `σ` be the least gap of
`I−P_j` off constants on nonsingleton components, or 1 if all components are
singletons. The proposed conclusion is, for every `k≥1`, `0<δ<1−v`,

\[
\Pr\{W_k\ge\lceil(v+\delta)k\rceil\}
\le\exp\!\left[-\frac{\sigma\delta^3k}{2048(1+\log d)}\right],
\qquad d=|A||B|. \tag{T}
\]

It is uniform over every repeated commuting strategy and passes to its
supremum without attainment. Connected support permits denominator 1024.
The exponent is conditional on the given graph gap; efficient sampling alone
does not acquire an inverse-polynomial gap. `ωᶜᵒ` cannot be replaced by a
smaller finite-tensor value without a separate theorem.
